text:
Kyle Palmieri tore his ACL on Nov. 28, 2025, and missed the rest of last season, ending a run of 223 straight games. At 35 he came back for camp, and through 19 games he is playing 16.7 minutes a night for the Islanders, his hometown team. The Smithtown native is still getting to the net.

The goals are what's missing. He has 3 on 5.93 expected goals, our measure of the quality of his chances, and none in his last eight games despite 2.9 expected goals in that stretch. His 7.9% shooting sits below his usual range of 9.4% to 14.2%, and our numbers flag him as due.

The underlying play holds up. New York has taken 54.3% of 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, 7.3 points more than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, over a small sample of eight games last season, had him on the end of plenty of passes across the slot or from behind the net, the looks that go in most often. This is a player who scored 30 and 24 goals in his last two full seasons. The chances say the finish is the only thing lagging.
headline: Palmieri is back from the ACL, and the chances are there
